doc.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Art Tatum as mentor and teaching at Aaron Copland School
summary: Tatum as concert pianist and mentor; Hanna trains students like Jeb Patton.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah that would be it. You know one of my mentors was Art Tatum. And he was truly a concert pianist. Whenever he played, no matter what he played, it was like a concert piece. And Horowitz — the violinist, I can’t think — anyway three famous concert musicians went into hear him play one night and they came away saying if this man had wanted to be a classical pianist he probably would have been the greatest classical pianist who ever lived. Because he would make up all that music on the spot. And still, this is like 45, almost 50 years after his death, there still hasn’t been anybody else to do that. So he was sort of a mentor to me. I said to myself I want to be able to do something like that. And I’ve been, at the Aaron Copland School of Music I’ve been training people to do just that. I have a young fellow by the name of Jeb Patton who is going to be in that same vein. A wonderful player. He plays with the Heath Brothers, you’ve probably seen him and haven’t noticed, but he’s in that same vein.
